Clarity.justification: The paper is exceptionally well-written with a logical structure: abstract, introduction clearly stating the regime assumption problem, related work, detailed methodology with design rationale tables, experimental setup, results with multiple diagnostic layers (AUROC, distributions, ROC curves, mechanism verification), discussion, and conclusion. Ideas such as stochastic hallucination vs. systematic confabulation are clearly articulated with equations (e.g., SMC-NLI formula) and specific examples from experiments (e.g., mean scores 0.6236 vs. 0.6299).

Novelty.justification: The paper presents the stochastic hallucination vs. systematic confabulation regime distinction as a prerequisite for sampling-based detectors, with empirical evidence on Llama-3-8B-Instruct and HaluEval QA showing chance-level AUROC (0.4933/0.4859). This is a notable advance over prior work (SelfCheckGPT, Semantic Uncertainty) validated only on base models/open-ended tasks, though the core negative result builds incrementally on RLHF distribution sharpening observations in related work.

Soundness.justification: Methods are sound and appropriate: dual-metric design (NLI + Embed), mechanism verification on 5 questions (scores vary in [0.3875,0.9853]), 14 unit tests, 10k real samples, 45k NLI pairs. Results are fully supported by data and consistent with provided code (AUROC 0.4933/0.4859, std 0.3388, per-label means differing by 0.006). No major flaws; implementation verified independently.

Significance.justification: Addresses a critical problem in uncertainty quantification for deployed instruction-tuned LLMs on factual QA. Contributions (C1-C4) including validated SMC infrastructure and benchmark validity concerns have practical impact for practitioners and define regime boundaries, though limited to one model/benchmark reduces broader lasting impact.

strengths: Rigorous multi-layer verification (unit tests, mechanism check, dual metrics) enabling clean attribution of negative result
Clear regime distinction with empirical falsification of consistency assumption (gap=0.006)
weaknesses: Evaluation limited to single model (Llama-3-8B-Instruct) and benchmark (HaluEval QA), acknowledged in limitations but reduces generalizability
Reliance on ChatGPT-derived labels introduces potential dataset-model mismatch confound
